Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

expose verb

reveal, bring to light: a plot, a fraud

also reveal, unmask, bring to light, show up, uncover (a plot), exposure, be exposed

classical

Ter. Phorm. 5.4.6 (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Cat. 3.15: Lentulus patefactus indiciīs

patefaciō, patefacere, patefēcī, patefactum

verb, third conjugation

disclose, expose, bring to light

Properly to throw open (a gate, a road); then to disclose a secret, expose a plot or a person: patefactus, found out, convicted (Cic. Cat. 3.15). Cicero pairs it with prōferre, bring forward (Mil. 103).

Other words

  • dētegō, dētegere, dētēxī, dētēctum — uncover; reveal, detect

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Liv. 27.16: īnsidiās (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Rud. 1.1.3: ventus dētēxit vīllam

    Properly to take the cover off, unroof (the wind took the roof off the farmhouse, Plaut. Rud. 1.1.3); then to reveal or detect a plot, a plan.

  • coarguō, coarguere, coarguī — show up, prove guilty

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fl. 11: vincī, refellī, coarguī (Lewis & Short); Cic. Verr. 2.4.104

    A word of the courts, most frequent in Cicero: to refute someone, prove him guilty.

Examples

  • sī hoc cēlātur, in metū, sīn patefit, in probrō sum

    if this is kept hidden, I live in fear; if it comes out, I’m disgracedTer. Phorm. 5.4.6 (Lewis & Short)

See also expose, uncover, show.

SourcesLewis & Short: patefacio · Lewis & Short: detego · Lewis & Short: coarguo
